title: Parallel: same voltage, split current
description: In parallel the branches share the battery voltage. Currents split. One dark lamp does not kill the other.

blocks.md:
## Two doors, same height

Parallel means each lamp has its own path across the same two battery points. Each lamp sees the full voltage. The currents add at the battery: I_total = I_A + I_B. A second lamp does not automatically steal the first lamp’s push.

This bites when you treat every extra lamp as a dimmer, or when you swap the series rules onto a split. Series shares V and keeps I the same. Parallel keeps V the same and splits I.

![Two lamps in parallel](assets/parallel-split.svg)

```text
battery --+--> lamp A -->+--> battery
          +--> lamp B -->+
same V on A and B · currents add
```

A common mistake is “adding a lamp always dims the first.” On a stiff battery the first lamp keeps its V. The questions ask you to keep those rules straight.

blocks.promptMd: Two lamps in parallel across one battery. Each lamp sees…

choices.md: Half the voltage, because they share like series
Less voltage because the other lamp steals it

blocks.explainMd: Parallel branches share V. They split I. A second lamp is another door, not a thief of height.

blocks.promptMd: If one parallel lamp is removed, the other lamp must go dark.
blocks.explainMd: Each branch is its own path. Opening one leaves the other.
